items.title: Fannie Mae Ups 2027 Mortgage Rate Forecast to 7.5%
items.author: Colin Robertson
items.content: Each month, Fannie Mae releases a forecast for home prices, sales, and mortgage rates, among other things. Between September’s report and October’s, they raised their estimate for the 30-year fixed a staggering 80 basis points (0.80%). The unusually large move reflects just how bad mortgage rates had it over the past month and change. But… Read More »

items.title: Mortgage Rates Keep Falling on AI Rout, But Will It Last?
items.author: Colin Robertson
items.content: Mortgage rates have now fallen for five days in a row. That puts the average 30-year fixed mortgage around 7.375%, a three-week low and roughly a quarter point below where they were earlier this month. items.title: Mortgage Rates Plummet Despite Hot Wholesale Inflation Report
items.author: Colin Robertson
items.content: Now it’s a party. A day after the mortgage rate rally seemed to end, then pulled off a miracle same-day turnaround, they’ve moved even lower still. items.title: Mortgage Rate Winning Streak Comes to an End
items.author: Colin Robertson
items.content: Well, what we didn’t want to happen, happened. We got a hotter-than-expected CPI report this morning, sending bond yields surging higher. After three straight days of slightly-better mortgage rates, there was some real promise we could make a more meaningful move back toward the low-7s. items.title: Mortgage Rates Move Lower as Oil Prices Cool Ahead of CPI Report

items.title: UWM Removes Minimum Credit Scores on Most Mortgages
items.author: Colin Robertson
items.content: The nation’s largest mortgage lender just got rid of its minimum credit score requirement on most home loans. The move is effective immediately and applies to conventional loans backed by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, as well as FHA, VA, and USDA loans. items.title: Mortgage Rate Relief Lasts All of One Day
items.author: Colin Robertson
items.content: Well that didn’t take long. One day after mortgage rates finally caught a much-needed break, bond yields are right back at new 52-week highs.
